# Corporate Security
Corporate Security protects corporate staff, property and research. It isn't a police force: on colony ground, colonial law and the colony's marshals come first. Security units turn out in regulation appearance.
## General security - [bold]Security Trainee[/bold]: new guard. - [bold]Security Officer[/bold]: 5 hours as a guard. - [bold]Senior Security Officer[/bold]: 25 hours as a guard. - [bold]Security Sergeant[/bold]: 25 hours as a guard. Leads the guard detail and reports to corporate management.
## Personal Protection Personal Protection is close protection for senior executives. It answers to the Personal Protection Coordinator, who answers to the senior executive. - [bold]Personal Protection Officer[/bold]: standard protection kit. - [bold]Personal Protection Specialist[/bold]: carries the detail's special weapon. - [bold]Personal Protection Coordinator[/bold]: leads the detail and can issue orders.
## Directorate Protection Directorate Protection guards members of the Directorate. It only deploys with them, as a third party.
## Rules - Guard corporate staff and property first. Don't go hunting. - Don't detain colonists on colony ground without the marshals, unless someone's life is in danger. - Corporate prisoners are handed to colonial authorities or held for transfer. They aren't held indefinitely. - Use of force has to be proportionate. Corporate liability follows every shot you fire.
